title: Salary Sacrifice Car Lease: How It Affects Your Hourly to Annual Conversion
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary, including salary sacrifice car lease, casual loading, super, and tax. Use our timesheet for accurate estimates.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours, before tax, super, and any salary sacrifice car lease arrangements.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is hourly × 1,976. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, super, and any salary sacrifice. Use our timesheet for an instant calculation.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of your base hourly rate, compensating for not receiving paid leave. For example, the minimum wage base of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour. Your annual gross is then based on the loaded rate. Super is paid on the loaded rate as well.

faqs.q: How does a salary sacrifice car lease affect my take-home pay?
faqs.a: A salary sacrifice car lease reduces your taxable income because the lease payments come from pre-tax salary. This lowers your income tax and Medicare levy. However, your super guarantee is still calculated on your ordinary earnings (including the sacrificed amount) up to the cap. Your take-home pay decreases by the lease amount, but you save tax. Use our take-home pay guide for estimates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you're offered an hourly rate or a salary, knowing your annual gross pay helps you plan. The basic formula is simple: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, that's hourly × 1,976. This article explains how to use that formula, what casual loading and super mean, and how a **salary sacrifice car lease** fits into the picture.

### The Standard 38-Hour Week

The Fair Work Ombudsman treats 38 hours as the ordinary full-time week. If you work 38 hours every week, your annual gross is hourly × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, that's $26.44 × 1,976 = $52,245.44 per year. But remember, this assumes no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. Use [the timesheet](/) to type your base hourly rate and see the annual figure.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. The Fair Work Commission sets the casual loading to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the minimum wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Never type a rate that already includes casual loading into the timesheet; instead, check the casual loading box to add it automatically. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It's not deducted from your pay; your employer adds it to a super fund. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year, so super stops once your earnings exceed that. For example, on $52,245 annual, super would be $6,269.40 (12% of $52,245). This is an estimate; see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Fortnightly Pay and Fortnightly Figures

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay times two. For a 38-hour week, weekly pay = hourly × 38. Fortnightly = hourly × 76. This helps when comparing to salary offers quoted per annum. The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) show full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 per week, which is about $108,352 per year. That's an average across all full-time employees, not a median for any specific job.

### Salary Sacrifice Car Lease: How It Works

A **salary sacrifice car lease** (also known as a novated lease) lets you pay for a car and its running costs from your pre-tax salary. This reduces your taxable income, so you pay less tax and Medicare levy. However, your super guarantee is still calculated on your ordinary earnings (which include the sacrificed amount) up to the maximum contribution base. When converting your hourly rate to annual, you need to consider the sacrifice amount. For example, if you earn $80,000 annually and sacrifice $10,000 for a car lease, your taxable income becomes $70,000. Your super (12%) would be based on $80,000 (ordinary earnings) up to the cap, but the sacrifice reduces your take-home pay. Use [pay guides](/blog) to understand how salary packaging interacts with your hourly rate.

The timesheet on this site does not deduct salary sacrifice; it shows gross pay before any packaging. To estimate your net after a salary sacrifice car lease, you would subtract the lease amount from your gross and then apply tax. The Australian Taxation Office provides the tax brackets for 2026–27: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on the next $26,800, 30% on the next $90,000, 37% on the next $55,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 not confirmed). This is an estimate only.

### Award Rates and Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. But many industries have award rates that are higher. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and vary by classification. Always check your specific award. The minimum wage is the floor; casual loading adds 25% to the base. Super is paid on top of the base rate (or the casual rate if applicable). For award rates, the same principles apply: hourly × hours × 52 gives annual, super on top, and casual loading if applicable. See [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) for more details.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

After you calculate your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident rates. For a single person claiming the tax-free threshold, tax is: 0 on first $18,200, then 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000, 30% on $45,001–$135,000, 37% on $135,001–$190,000, 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy adds 2% (subject to reduction thresholds). This does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed estimate, see [take-home pay](/topics/take-home).

### Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) is the home page. You type your base hourly rate. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top. The timesheet then shows your annual gross (hourly × 38 × 52), your weekly and fortnightly pay, and an estimate of tax and super. It assumes 38 hours per week. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. The timesheet does not include salary sacrifice; that's a separate calculation.

### Summary

Converting hourly to annual is straightforward: hourly × hours per week × 52. For full-time, assume 38 hours. Casual loading adds 25% to the base rate. Super is 12% on top, up to the cap. A **salary sacrifice car lease** reduces your taxable income but not your super base (up to the cap). Use the timesheet to get started, and refer to [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for more detailed figures. Remember, this is an estimate; always consult a professional for your specific situation.
